module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Zariski Cancellation

*Reference:* [arxiv/2208.14736](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.14736)
**The Zariski Cancellation Problem and related problems in Affine Algebraic Geometry**
by *Neena Gupta*
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Arxiv.«2208.14736»

open Polynomial

/--
A finitely generated `k`-algebra `A` is cancellative if for all finitely generated `k` algebras `B` such that
`B[X] ≅ₖ A[X]` we have `B ≅ₖ A`.
-/
def IsCancellative (k A : Type*) [Field k]
    [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Algebra.FiniteType k A] : Prop := ∀ {B : Type*}
    [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra.FiniteType k B], Nonempty (A[X] ≃ₐ[k] B[X]) →
    Nonempty (A ≃ₐ[k] B)

/--
The **Zariski Cancellation Problem**: every polynomial ring over a field `k` of characteristic
`0` is cancellative.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem {k : Type*} [Field k]
    [CharZero k] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] : IsCancellative k (MvPolynomial ι k) := by
  sorry

/--
The single variable polynomial ring `k[X]` is cancellative in any characteristic
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem.variants.dim_one
    {k : Type*} [Field k] : IsCancellative k k[X] := by
  sorry

/--
The two variable polynomial ring `k[X]` is cancellative in any characteristic
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem.variants.dim_two {k : Type*} [Field k] :
    IsCancellative k (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k) := by
  sorry

/--
The positive characteristic case of the Zariski Cancellation Problem is false in dimension `3`
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 13 14]
theorem zariski_cancellation_problem.variants.false_pos_card
    (p : ℕ) [hp : Fact p.Prime] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (hι : Fintype.card ι = 3) :
    ¬ IsCancellative (ZMod p) (MvPolynomial ι (ZMod p)) := by
  sorry

end Arxiv.«2208.14736»

findings.description: The docstring says "The two variable polynomial ring `k[X]` is cancellative in any characteristic". `k[X]` is the one-variable ring; it looks copied from `dim_one`. The Lean statement is correct: `IsCancellative k (MvPolynomial (Fin 2) k)` is the claim for $k[X,Y]$ over an arbitrary field. Only the docstring is wrong.
findings.source_evidence: arXiv 2208.14736, Section 2: "an affirmative answer to Question 1′ for the case n=2 ... over perfect fields of arbitrary characteristic by P. Russell. Later, it has been shown that even the hypothesis of perfect field can be dropped ([BG3])", and "the cancellation property of k[X, Y]". BG3 is titled "A note on the cancellation property of k[X, Y]" (J. Algebra Appl. 14(9) (2015) 1540007).
findings.suggested_fix: /-- The two variable polynomial ring $k[X, Y]$ is cancellative over any field $k$ (any characteristic). -/

findings.description: The variant asserts `¬ IsCancellative (ZMod p) (MvPolynomial ι (ZMod p))` for `card ι = 3`, i.e. only over the prime fields F_p. The cited result, and the natural reading of the docstring ("The positive characteristic case of the Zariski Cancellation Problem is false in dimension 3"), cover every field of positive characteristic. The Lean statement is true: it is a special case of Gupta's theorem, and it still gives a counterexample in each characteristic p. But it is strictly weaker than the source's result. Restricting to prime fields is defensible, so this is not a misformalization; a maintainer may still want the general form.
findings.source_evidence: Gupta, Invent. Math. 195 (2014) 279–288 (arXiv 1208.0483), abstract: "We show that the Cancellation Conjecture does not hold for the affine space A^3_k over any field k of positive characteristic." Survey 2208.14736: "In [G1] and [G3], the author settled the Zariski Cancellation Problem (Question 1′) completely for affine spaces in positive characteristic."
findings.suggested_fix: theorem zariski_cancellation_problem.variants.false_pos_char {k : Type*} [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (hι : Fintype.card ι = 3) : ¬ IsCancellative k (MvPolynomial ι k). Alternatively keep the ZMod p version and say in the docstring that it is the prime-field special case.

reformulations.difference: The source defines cancellative as: for any k-algebra B, A[X] ≅_k B[X] implies A ≅_k B. The Lean definition only quantifies over finitely generated B (`[Algebra.FiniteType k B]`), and B lives in a separate universe parameter. Relatedly, the main theorem phrases Question 1′ ("B[X] ≅ k[X_1..X_{n+1}] ⇒ B ≅ k[X_1..X_n]") as `IsCancellative k (MvPolynomial ι k)`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A is finitely generated over k, so A[X] is too, and hence so is any B[X] ≅_k A[X]. B is the image of B[X] under the surjective k-algebra map X ↦ 0 (`(aeval 0).restrictScalars k`), so B is finitely generated. The hypothesis therefore holds automatically. Proved in Lean: `IsCancellative.{u,v,w} k A ↔ IsCancellativeSrc.{u,v,w} k A`, using `Algebra.FiniteType.trans`, `.equiv` and `.of_surjective`. On universes: the positive theorems are universe-polymorphic in B's universe, so they include the case where that universe is large enough to hold every finitely generated k-algebra. The negated variant holds in every universe via `ULift` of a Type-0 counterexample. For Question 1′: (MvPolynomial ι k)[X] ≅_k k^{[n+1]}. The extra case n = 0 (empty ι) is true: an iso B[X] ≅ k[X] carries B = B^* ∪ {0} onto k^* ∪ {0} = k.

review.notes: No misformalization found. The main theorem `zariski_cancellation_problem` faithfully states Question 1′ of the survey over fields of characteristic zero, which the survey identifies as the open case ("The ZCP is still a challenging problem in characteristic zero"). It includes n = 0, 1, 2, which are true. `research open` is still accurate: none of the 2024–2026 arXiv papers I found settles the question for affine spaces; they address the generalized problem for other varieties. The survey poses ZCP as a question, and the file states the affirmative answer as a plain theorem rather than `answer(sorry) ↔ ...`. That is a style choice, not a mathematical defect; Gupta's own Inventiones abstract calls it the "Cancellation Conjecture". The solved variants are correct and correctly tagged. `dim_one` follows from Abhyankar–Eakin–Heinzer over any field, as summarized in the survey. `dim_two` follows from Fujita/Miyanishi–Sugie/Russell plus Bhatwadekar–Gupta 2015 for non-perfect fields. `false_pos_card` follows from Gupta 2014 via the Asanuma threefold, which exists over every F_p (e.g. X^2Y+Z^4+T+T^6 for p=2). The name `false_pos_card` presumably means "char"; that is only naming. For `dim_one` I relied on the survey's account of the AEH result rather than the 1972 paper itself.
